group_assessment.weighting: This is the primary group for both the gene and the disease, and 47% of its output is on WWOX — the inverse of yesterday's paper, where lipid expertise was deep and gene expertise borrowed. Observation and interpretation therefore carry closer to the same weight here, with one asymmetry that runs the other way: a group this invested in a gene is the least likely to under-read its own rescue. That is precisely why the untested WT-versus-rescued comparisons in the figures matter, and why the reviewers' n=3 objection is recorded even though it cannot be quoted.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: PMCID PMC8649866, CC BY 4.0, in the PMC open-access subset: oa.fcgi returns a record with license="CC BY" and retracted="no". Full JATS XML, figures, appendix and review process file are all retrievable.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No locator is abstract-anchored and none could be. The abstract reports that neuronal restoration reverses the phenotypes; every proposition below is a bound on that claim — the P0-only window, the 60-70% transduction, the untested WT-versus-rescued comparisons, the doubled unmyelinated axon count, the qualifiers on the tumour survey, the anaesthetic, n=3. These are exactly what an abstract drops. Verified mechanically: all sixteen snippets match the body and none matches the abstract.

entries.proposition: The authors frame the work as a proof of concept aimed at a clinical trial in WOREE and SCAR12.
entries.snippet: this proof‐of‐concept will lay down the groundwork for a possible gene therapy clinical trial on children suffering from the devastating and often refractory WOREE and SCAR12 syndromes
entries.anchor: Discussion, closing paragraph

entries.proposition: The unmet need the argument starts from: current antiepileptics fail these children.

entries.proposition: Transduction reaches 60-70% of neurons, not near-completeness — the efficacy is achieved with a partially transduced brain.

entries.proposition: Oligodendrocytes are never transduced, which is what makes the myelin rescue non-cell-autonomous rather than a direct effect.
entries.snippet: WWOX expression was lacking in non‐neuronal cells of the brain such as oligodendrocytes
entries.anchor: Results, same section, verified by CC1/anti-WWOX co-staining

entries.proposition: PREMISE_TAG — every efficacy number is conditioned on treatment at P0, and the authors state the reason and the untested alternative. In WOREE, diagnosis follows seizure onset by months.
entries.snippet: The limited life span and poor conditions of Wwox‐null mice prompted us to treat these mice very early on in their life (P0)
entries.anchor: Discussion, penultimate paragraph

entries.proposition: The later-window experiment is declared as future work, not as done. REVIVAL_TRIGGER: a post-natal dosing result would change the reading of the whole paper.

entries.anchor: Discussion, penultimate paragraph

entries.proposition: The authors themselves record that the rescue is incomplete and attribute the residue to an oligodendrocyte-autonomous WWOX function.
entries.snippet: there are still some differences between rescued and WT mice which could be attributed to an oligodendrocyte‐specific WWOX function in regulating the myelination process
entries.anchor: Discussion, third paragraph

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE PANEL — in the electron-microscopy figure the only comparison drawn between WT and rescued animals is the unmyelinated axon count, and it is significant AGAINST the rescue: roughly 26 per field in WT versus roughly 52 in the treated mice, marked **. In the two panels where the rescue looks strongest (myelinated axons per field, corpus callosum ~130/46/105 and optic nerve ~140/68/124) the brackets run WT-vs-KO and KO-vs-rescued, never WT-vs-rescued, so the visible residual gap is untested. The g-ratio scatter does normalise: the treated cloud overlies WT while the KO cloud sits flat at 0.8-0.95.

entries.proposition: INFERENZA, not DATO — the convergence with FT-039. Restoring WWOX only in neurons rescued peripheral phenotypes (glucose, fertility, bone) with no peripheral WWOX expression, while yesterday's reading showed the liver-specific knockout failing to reproduce the whole-body HDL phenotype. Two groups, two directions, one shape: for several WWOX phenotypes the tissue where the readout is measured is not the tissue where the gene must be present. Neither paper tests the other's organ.
